Save places by address, rename them, and never replace or forget silently
mapbox-nav 03
e4bf26e2 · 25 files
tag_place takes an optional address: it is looked up and the RESOLVED address plus its point are saved, and the result reads that address back. Several matches or none save nothing and say so (candidates listed); no lookup service or no connection refuses in words. Without an address the current fix is saved and reverse looked up; a failed lookup still saves by coordinates and says the address is unknown. Lookups use Android's Geocoder, not the Mapbox Search SDK: Mapbox ToS 2.7.2 forbids storing temporary geocodes, and mapbox-nav ticket 03 ruled "nothing from Mapbox is stored". PlaceGeocoder is the seam. rename_place (new) keeps coordinates and address; over the engine it is one POST that also moves place reminders, otherwise reminders move via NotesController. Refuses when the new name is taken. forget_place, and a save that would move an existing label more than 150 m, now write nothing unless confirmed, returning what would be lost (the clear_codes shape). Voice audit 2026-10-09 finding 2. Saved places screen (moved out of FleetScreen.kt) gains save by address with a match picker, replace and delete confirms, rename, and the address under each label - all through the same PlaceController calls (ADR 0035). Voice guide copy updated. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Web revamp 15: push notifications, the client half
web-revamp 15
22cbfd4c · 108 files
The service worker is now hand-written (vite-plugin-pwa injectManifest, src/sw.ts) so it can show a notification. It keeps every rule the generated one had: skipWaiting and clientsClaim (206af39), /api/ NetworkOnly and never written to a cache, and the navigation denylist that mirrors Django's own prefixes. The precache was the same 72 entries before and after the swap. - push: shows the engine's payload as sent, with a "Turn these off" action; an unreadable payload still shows something, saying so, because a browser cancels a subscription whose pushes show nothing. - notificationclick: opens or focuses the payload page (same origin only, a window already open is reused); the action POSTs /api/push/preferences/off with the session cookie and then says what the engine said, or that nothing was changed, never before the engine answered. - All of it is plain functions in lib/push-sw.ts, tested without a worker. - /settings/notifications: the iOS three-step install card when not standalone (checked before asking the browser, since Safari tabs have no PushManager), "Notifications are not set up on this server." when the engine has no keys, its own sentence for a denied permission, subscribe and unsubscribe (the engine is told first on the way off, and the browser undoes its own subscription if the engine refuses on the way on), three kind switches, the morning time, and a master off. The copy is held to the compulsion test by a vitest over every string and over what renders. - Devices now says "Last seen", not "last used": any request counts, the phone's background sync included (research note docs/design/settings-notifications-devices.md). Tests: 491 (434 before this commit, 378 before 05), from vitest's JSON reporter. `npm run push-sw` drives the BUILT sw.js in real Chromium: it activates, shows a push delivered through the DevTools protocol, handles "Turn these off" against the fake engine, and never caches /api/. Shots kept under .scratch/web-revamp/research/shots/15/. Owed on live (Kevin): VAPID keys, the schedule installed, Mia subscribing on her iPhone, a real push arriving. ADR 0052 built. events and checklists gain owner_user_id (null is shared) and created_by_id; checklist_items gains created_by_id. Both are set from the request, never from a body, and never go on the wire: the serializers render visibility shared|private instead. - household.tenancy.visible() is the choke point: scoped() plus the member filter, with items, ticks and skips joining through their parent. Every read and write path for the five tables uses it: api/events.py, checklists/views.py, api/changes.py and the MCP list tools (MCP writes already run the routed views). Another member's private row is a 404. - List routes and the changes feed carry a row private to someone else as a redacted tombstone (id, deleted_at, updated_at, redacted), so a replica that held it while shared drops it. Items and ticks also tombstone when their parent turned private, using the later of the two instants. - Who may change: owner may share; a shared row may be made private by its creator, or by anyone when no creator is recorded; otherwise 403 "Only the person who added this can make it private." - Removing a member tombstones their private rows in the same transaction and keeps them private. - The database refuses an owner who is not a member of the row's household. Trigger, not the ticket's composite FK: a composite FK would null the owner on member removal and turn their tombstones into shared full rows in the feed. - source_credentials.user (backfilled to a household's single owner), set by whoever hands a session over; upsert_canvas_task takes p_owner_user and inserts Canvas rows private to that member. engine-mcp 10: /mcp inside Django, an 11-tool registry, read and write, off by default
engine-mcp 10
134144eb · 18 files
The engine answers MCP at /mcp on the official SDK (mcp==2.2.0, pinned with its transitive deps), driven once per request from the WSGI view: stateless, JSON responses, no session id. Tools run on the request thread, so they use the request's own DB connection. - Off unless LEGION_MCP=on; off answers 404 in words. - Device tokens only; a read-scoped token is refused by every write tool in words, and again by IsHouseholdMember inside the dispatched view. - Writes resolve and call the routed REST view, so serializers, tenancy and the gate's 405 are the REST ones. Gated tables unwritable, memory tables excluded, no ingestion tool, no mail. - Every failure is isError with words; reads say provenance and estimates in words; empty is distinguished from unreadable. - Throttled per token (LEGION_MCP_RATE, default 60/min); every call audited in public.mcp_calls (token, method, tool, outcome; never arguments or results), listed in TENANT_TABLES. - The tenancy leak test covers every tool from both households. Server suite: 1249 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 44 skipped (JUnit XML). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The phone follows the engine's keyset and knows when a read is complete
no ticket
ef6b47ad · 4 files
EngineSyncedTable sends ?after= when the engine hands back next_after, so a page of rows sharing one timestamp is followed past instead of re-served. An engine without next_after gets byte-for-byte the old loop. fetchEverything reports whether the read reached next: null. LedgerBackend.fetchTransactionSet carries that verdict (complete = false by default, so Supabase can never delete by absence); DjangoLedgerBackend overrides it from the page loop. Synced list routes page with a keyset, so the full ledger list is readable
no ticket
08d6ccb5 · 10 files
The gate writes every line of one statement with one created_at, so a table keyed on created_at could fill a 500-row page with a single timestamp. next then repeated its own cursor and a client following the documented loop stopped early, holding a truncated table. That was survivable while the phone only inserted what was missing; it is not once the phone treats the full list as the set. paginate_keyset orders by (cursor, pk) and returns next_after (the last row's id) beside the unchanged next; ?after= continues strictly after that position. A client that sends only since gets exactly the old read, so installed APKs are unaffected. The memory list's copy of the base list uses the same helper. openapi.yaml and the web's schema.d.ts are regenerated. The deletion contract for ledger_transactions is written on its viewset: the full list is the set, and a client may treat an absent row as deleted only when its read reached next: null. Tests cover the categoriser from the previous commit and the paging here. Kevin: "i want a quick toggle button to mute all notifications and put the phone on vibrate only", then "i want it on the home screen beside apps". On: the ringer goes to vibrate and LEGION's own Do Not Disturb mode comes on. Calls from anyone and alarms get through, as vibration. Every other notification is silent but still lands in the shade. Off: the ringer goes back to what it was before, not to a default. It uses its own AutomaticZenRule, not the system DND switch, because setNotificationPolicy rewrites the user's DND policy, and a toggle that quietly clobbers someone's DND setup is worse than no toggle. Kevin: "the phone has a long press side button to summon ai assistant. can we make it open the live conversation? a single input. so it wont continue listening after i say something." MainActivity now handles ACTION_ASSIST (and the older VOICE_COMMAND), which makes LEGION eligible for Android's assistant role. No VoiceInteractionService was needed: on the A25, `cmd role add-role-holder android.app.role.ASSISTANT` accepted it. Samsung's side-key long-press was already set to "digital assistant app", a slot filled by whoever holds that role, so no Samsung setting changed. The intent goes to the service as ASSIST_ONE_SHOT and on to LiveSessionController.onAssistRequest. One-shot reuses dismissAfterTurn, the after-the-reply hang-up that "that will be all" uses, so the answer finishes before the socket closes. The decision lives in OneShotGate (pure, tested): a conversation that opens with a greeting ends a turn before the user has spoken, so the hang-up arms only on the first turn end after the mic opens. Holding the key during a live conversation doesn't cut it off; it ends after the next answer. A plain tap disarms it. OneShotGateTest covers greeting first, mic first, firing once, plain tap, disarm, speak-only turns, and mid-conversation. 3588 tests, 0 failures from the JUnit XML. On the A25 (APK hash matched), a simulated long-press logged "powerLongPress packageName=Digital Assistant (com.kevin.legion)", then START act=ASSIST into MainActivity, onTap, and mic_open. Owed: the hang-up after one answer needs someone to speak, and nothing here can. The gate is tested but the on-phone behaviour is not yet observed. Background location stops powering the GPS chip
no ticket
0f1eb8bc · 4 files
After the restart, `dumpsys location` on the A25 showed LEGION as the only reason the GPS radio was on around the clock: GPS_PROVIDER, HIGH_ACCURACY, every 30s (mFixInterval=30000). Every other app asked passively or at low power. The code called this mode "battery-friendly". A 100 m distance filter doesn't let the chip sleep, because the chip has to compute a fix to learn whether you moved 100 m. That habit dates from the head unit, when the car paid for the power. Background now uses the network provider (Wi-Fi/cell, nearly free) and the passive provider, which takes any fix another app already paid for. GPS comes on only in fast mode, for a screen that needs live position, and goes off when that screen releases it. Seeding from a cached fix still reads the GPS provider, since reading doesn't power the chip. Kevin accepted the trade-off: "agreed do the gps fix". Place-arrival triggers now run on network accuracy (~20-100 m in town) against 150 m arrival zones, and may lag or miss somewhere with no Wi-Fi nearby. LocationControllerBackgroundTest pins it at the LocationManager boundary: nothing is registered on GPS after init, network and passive are, and fast mode turns GPS on and releasing it turns it back off. 3575 tests, 0 failures from the JUnit XML. Owed: the phone dropped off ADB before the install. Still to confirm that LEGION leaves the GPS request list in dumpsys location while idle. A resume that never connects discards its handle
no ticket
7297442b · 6 files
Kevin, 2026-09-27: "why does the voice agent says no connection retry? i cant talk at all" logcat: session_start, then "session_end: BidiGenerateContent session not found". The server had expired a session and LEGION kept sending its resume handle. That handle lives only in memory and was cleared on a user stop but never on this close, so every tap resent the same dead handle and failed identically. For a foreground service that means voice is gone for days. The chip said NO CONNECTION because it never connected. Force-stopping the app on the phone dropped the handle and voice came back at once. The fix: a close with no successful connect clears the handle. Costs one conversation's continuity, which is less than losing the voice path. The ranking is the design, and it is by when a thing stops being possible, never by which table it came from. Overdue first, with the MOST overdue leading - something ignored longest is more likely forgotten than deferred. Then dated, soonest first. Then undated errands. Then today's already-ticked lines, listed last rather than dropped, because a finished day should read as finished rather than as empty: section 1's empty-versus-unreadable distinction pointed at a day's work. A checklist line is never overdue. It resets tonight, so it cannot be late, only unticked - and conflating the two would put a bio line it is still 9am to do in the same bucket as a coursework deadline that passed, which is the exact flattening this module exists to avoid. A checklist that cannot be READ is skipped rather than rendered as an empty one, for the same reason. The judgement is pure and the fetching is not: Outstanding.kt has no Android in it and carries every ordering decision, OutstandingController only gathers. That split is what lets ten tests pin the ranking without Room or a device, including the failure this exists to prevent - three lists stapled end to end, so an undated errand outranks a deadline that passed purely because of which table it came from. 3518 tests, 0 failures. Owed: nothing calls it yet. It is the input the advisor and a screen should both read, and wiring either is the next step rather than part of this one. /api/changes dropped every aspect but the last, so the calendar was always empty

Kevin's Today screen said "Nothing on the calendar today" while the database held 467 events. It said it every day. `aspects` is declared in openapi.yaml as `type: array` with no style/explode. OpenAPI's default for a query array is explode: true - repeated params, `?aspects=events&aspects=checklists`. The generated TypeScript client sent exactly that. This endpoint read `query_params.get("aspects")`, which returns only the LAST occurrence, so a client obeying the published contract asked for events and checklists and received `["checklists"]`. The server was wrong, not the client. The spec said repeated; the implementation only ever read comma-separated. It failed silently and in the worst direction: a 200 with no `events` key, which renders as "nothing on the calendar" and is indistinguishable from a household that genuinely has nothing on. Checklists worked the whole time, which is what made it look like a calendar problem rather than a query-string problem. Fixed by accepting BOTH rather than narrowing the spec and regenerating clients: getlist picks up every repeated occurrence and each is still comma-split, so the documented form keeps working and mixed spellings work too. Found by querying the API by hand from the browser once the screen and the data disagreed. Three wrong guesses came first and each was discarded on evidence: I grepped the built CSS for "min-width: 768px" and called a missing breakpoint the bug (Tailwind v4 emits "@media (width>=48rem)" - the responsive rules were complete); I suspected the day bucketing (the app's own arithmetic put the row on today correctly); and I suspected the service worker again (the new build was loading). The query string was the last difference left. 13 tests in test_changes_api.py. The new one pins the repeated form, the comma form, and the two mixed - a contract mismatch that returns a cheerful 200 is worse than one that 400s. A PWA on a home screen or a tab left open can hold it for days. Nothing errors - the app just keeps serving the previous build, so a deploy looks like it did nothing. Safe here because /api/ is NetworkOnly: taking over mid-session can swap the shell under a user, but it can never serve a cached figure, which is what CLAUDE.md section 4 actually cares about. The shell may be stale, the data may not. I was wrong twice on the way to this and both are worth recording. I first grepped the built CSS for "min-width: 768px", found nothing, and said I had found the bug - Tailwind v4 emits "@media (width>=48rem)", so the responsive rules were there all along. The md:flex / md:hidden / md:flex-row declarations are complete and correct. Grepping for a syntax the tool does not emit and reading the absence as a finding is how you invent a bug. Kevin, 2026-09-11: "the AI doesnt see anything thats due on sunday for sch. i asked it and it didnt know." Seven were due that night. read_calendar queried EventKind.EVENT. Every assignment is EventKind.TASK. On the A25 that is 145 of 314 rows, and no tool in the toolbox returned one of them - read_list is reminders, manage_checklist is checklists, and NotesController.openAppointments is TASK-filtered but exists to match a spoken title for manage_item, not to read a day. Assignments were unreachable by voice entirely, which makes it an ADR 0035 gap as well: not a weak hands path, none. It failed in the worst available way. An empty window reads as "you have nothing due", which is indistinguishable from the truth. The first diagnosis was wrong and the ticket keeps it, because how it was wrong is the useful part. I had a timezone theory: Canvas writes an 11:59pm local deadline as 04:59Z the NEXT day, so every Sunday deadline carries a Monday UTC date, and this codebase has already been bitten by exactly that once (2026-09-01, "the due dates seem to be advanced by 1 day"). Plausible, and false. Pulling the Room database settled it in one query: allDay=0, a true instant, and activeByKindInLocalWindow was bucketing them onto the correct local day all along. The storage was never broken. I had also reached the right answer first and talked myself out of it, on two pieces of evidence that were both wrong. The advisor now writes a real recurring checklist through AdvisorProposalExecutor's allowlisted create_checklist op, stamped with a sourceKey, and finds the same row again by that key. A migration bug that would have shipped, caught by writing the migration test. MIGRATION_68_69 read `ADD COLUMN sourceKey TEXT DEFAULT NULL`. SQLite records that as the literal string NULL - PRAGMA table_info reports dflt_value = 'NULL' - while Room's generated v69 schema declares plain `sourceKey TEXT` with no default. Room validates the migrated table against that schema when it opens the database, so this was not cosmetic: it fails the upgrade for every existing install with "Migration didn't properly handle checklists". A nullable column already defaults to NULL; saying so explicitly is what broke it. The DEFAULT clause is gone. The test compares against the LIVE generated JSON rather than a hand-written expectation, and builds its v68 starting table from 68.json for the same reason - a hand-transcribed expectation agrees with a hand-written migration for exactly as long as both are wrong in the same way, which is precisely what happened here. Four callers survived the deleted class and each needed a different answer. GoalPlanAgent and the wellbeing digest both called materializeToday first and read back second. There is nothing to materialise now - a recurring checklist simply exists - so the first call is gone rather than replaced. The digest reads through the same source key, and an unreadable checklist throws to its existing wellbeing_digest_read_failed event rather than quietly becoming "nothing on your plan tonight". NotesController's allItems filter STAYS, as a tombstone. Nothing writes a "Plan: " row any more, so on a clean install it matches nothing - but the migration deliberately leaves already-TICKED legacy rows where they are (ticket 04: "a done row is a record of a day that already happened"). Those survivors were hidden from the Inbox and the day view before the migration, and dropping the filter would surface a pile of old machine-written lines on the first launch after upgrading: a visible regression produced by a cleanup. GoalChecklistPanel is REPOINTED, not deleted, and ticket 04 was wrong about it. That resolution said to delete the panel because the calendar day view already rendered the same thing. By the time this was built, ticket 02's HOME restructure had removed that call site and BodyScreen was the only caller left - where the panel also hosts the relocated TRAINING affordances, + LOG SET and the exercise drilldown. Deleting it would have taken log_workout_set's hands path with it, which is the exact ADR 0035 failure ticket 02 exists to prevent, one screen over. So the panel stayed and its DATA moved, which is what ticket 04 actually decided. The ticket is amended in place rather than left reading as if it had been obeyed. Signup, invite codes and the household an owner administers
web-and-households 03
1c80d735 · 18 files
web-and-households ticket 03, the rest of it. The session/CSRF slice landed this morning in 64004e7; this is everything that was deferred out of it, and it sits on top rather than replacing any of it. Kevin, 2026-09-10: "we need to build the browser/mobile wrapper with household creation and user signup etc." His wife joins the existing household with a join code; his parents get a create-household code, which is the reason codes exist at all rather than one hardcoded household. The model - Invite: code, household (nullable), creates_household, created_by, max_uses, used_count, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at. Migration household/0003_invite.py, plus a CHECK constraint shipped by that migration - an invite either joins a household that exists or creates one, and CLAUDE.md section 7 puts an integrity rule that must hold when Django has a bug in SQL rather than in Python. - The code is twelve base64url characters from `secrets`, generated the way the ticket specifies. `Invite.mint()` returns it alongside the row, the same shape `DeviceToken.issue` uses, and `__str__` deliberately does not contain it so it cannot leak into an admin log or a traceback. It IS stored in the clear, unlike a device key, and the class docstring says why: an owner re-shares a live code and `/api/auth/invite/<code>` describes one before it is spent, and neither is possible against a hash. `Invite.find` compares with `secrets.compare_digest` after the indexed lookup - which changes no outcome under Postgres's byte-exact default collation, and is there because a credential comparison that rests on a collation setting is one nobody re-checks when the setting changes. The endpoints - POST /api/auth/signup. Validates the code, creates the user, joins or founds a household, issues a device token like login does, 201. Its own `signup` throttle scope at 5/min rather than sharing `login`, so a burst of signup attempts cannot lock the household out of signing in. The whole handler is one transaction and takes a row lock on the invite (`Invite.find(for_update=True)`), which is what makes max_uses real: without it two people redeeming the last use both read used_count before either writes. `for_update` drops the select_related, because Postgres refuses FOR UPDATE against the nullable side of an outer join and `household` is nullable here by design. - LEGION_OPEN_SIGNUP (settings, .env.example, off by default and no required_env - an operator who has not thought about it must get the closed behaviour). On, a request with no invite_code founds a household. A request that DOES carry a code is still honoured either way: the ticket's "always creates a household" is read as describing the codeless path, because the other reading leaves an open-signup engine unable to add a second adult to a household at all. - GET /api/auth/invite/<code>. Says whether a code is live, whether it joins or founds, and - only when it joins - the household's NAME, never its id. Spends nothing. Ticket 05's /join/<code> screen is the caller. Shares the `signup` throttle scope, so previewing and redeeming give a stranger five guesses a minute between them rather than five each. Unknown code 404s, a real-but-dead code answers 200 with live:false and a reason in words. - GET/PATCH /api/households/me, POST/GET/DELETE /api/households/me/invites, DELETE /api/households/me/members/<user_id>, in household/households.py under a new /api/households/ mount. GET is open to any member (a member who could not see the roster could not check they joined the right family); the other four are owner-only through a new IsHouseholdOwner, which guards exactly those membership verbs and no data route. - Removing a member revokes their live device tokens AND the invites they minted. The second is beyond the ticket's table and is the same failure one step removed: a removed person keeping a live code keeps a back door. Their User row survives with no household, so IsHouseholdMember refuses every request a surviving session makes. The last owner cannot be removed, themself included, and it refuses in words - a household with no owner has nobody who can ever invite or remove anyone again and no admin above it. - GET /api/auth/devices and DELETE /api/auth/devices/<id>: a member lists and revokes their OWN live tokens, never a key, and another person's token id 404s rather than 403s. - manage.py create_household --name --owner-email [--password] [--id], for the compose bootstrap path. Refuses to re-home somebody already in a household, and warns when the engine crosses from one household to two, because that is the moment add_household_member and the superuser signal stop being able to guess. No household field on /api/auth/me, and that is one row of the ticket's own table not built as written. tests/test_tenancy.py's test_no_openapi_component_declares_household_id forbids any component declaring `household` or `household_id`; it caught the first attempt this morning and 64004e7 reverted it. GET /api/households/me carries the household id because it IS the household resource, which is a different thing. The ticket body now says so where the table is. Tests: 52 in tests/test_accounts.py - signup with a join code, with a create code (first use founds, second use joins what it founded), spent, expired, revoked and unknown codes, an email already taken, a weak password, the throttle, open signup off and on and still honouring a code, the preview endpoint on live/dead/unknown codes, owner-versus-member on every owner-only route, member removal revoking tokens and invites, the last-owner refusal, the device list and revoke, both directions of the tenancy check (a signup into a founded household sees none of household A's rows, and a join-code signup sees all of them), and the five create_household paths. Every refusal asserts the absence of what was not created, not just the status code. Full suite from the JUnit XML, never the console: 759 tests, 717 passed, 42 skipped, 0 failures, 0 errors. Before this commit the same suite was 707 tests, 665 passed, 42 skipped (64004e7's message reports that run as "707 tests ... 42 skipped"). +52 is exactly this file. openapi.yaml regenerated with manage.py write_openapi, and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts with openapi-typescript. Not verified: nothing here has run against a deployed engine or through a browser. The /join/<code> screen that consumes the preview endpoint is ticket 05 and does not exist yet.
